items.stem: Your context window is fixed and the knowledge base is large. What is the best general strategy?

options.text: Retrieve and include only the most relevant context, budgeting the window across its parts
options.rationale: Correct: relevance-driven, budgeted assembly uses the window effectively.

options.text: Always fill the window with as much text as possible
options.rationale: Stuffing irrelevant text wastes the budget and can dilute relevance.

options.text: Include the entire knowledge base every call
options.rationale: That is impossible under a fixed window and wasteful.

options.text: Send only the user's last message with no retrieval
options.rationale: Dropping relevant context harms answer quality.

items.explanation: Correct: relevance-driven, budgeted assembly uses the window effectively.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Which TWO practices reduce cost and latency without losing needed context? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Cache stable context so it is not re-sent unchanged every turn
options.rationale: Correct: caching avoids repeated cost for unchanged context.

options.text: Summarise or compress long history while keeping key facts
options.rationale: Correct: compression preserves signal while shrinking tokens.

options.text: Re-fetch and re-send all context on every request
options.rationale: Re-sending unchanged context wastes cost and time.

options.text: Always use the maximum context window regardless of need
options.rationale: Maximal context raises cost and latency needlessly.

items.explanation: Correct: caching avoids repeated cost for unchanged context.
items.provenance: original Mastemy item drafted by an AI agent; no external question source

items.stem: Retrieved documents sometimes contain text like 'ignore previous instructions'. How should the system treat retrieved content?

options.text: As untrusted data that must not be executed as instructions
options.rationale: Correct: treating retrieved text as data defends against prompt injection.

options.text: As trusted system instructions to follow
options.rationale: Following injected instructions is the vulnerability itself.

options.text: As higher priority than the system prompt
options.rationale: Retrieved data must never override the system prompt.

options.text: As safe because it came from the knowledge base
options.rationale: Source does not make embedded instructions safe.

items.explanation: Correct: treating retrieved text as data defends against prompt injection.
